title: مخزن الادویه (Makhzan al-Adviyah, Persian materia medica)
shelf_note: A lithographed Persian materia medica (the drug-name glossary at the back of the book) held in medical-heritage collections (McGill Osler, Toronto, Medical Heritage Library). It belongs on that shelf.
structure_note: The structure counts give pages_translated 0, but the pages_translated field says 731 and this page has a translation, so the counters disagree (E2). Only 145 of 778 pages carry a printed number, with 43 backsteps and 15 repeats. That is probably not a splice. The glossary at the back has its own pagination (this leaf, record 758, prints '۵۴' while the OCR says '۵۳'), and Persian numerals on a lithograph get misread, which together would produce backsteps and repeats.

pages.layout: lithographed Nastaliq; a central box of five vertical columns of drug-name entries, with dense diagonal marginal text on the top, right and bottom; running head at the top; page number in a diamond in the right margin

ocr_errors.image: Long blocks of diagonal marginal text fill the top, right and bottom (more than 30 slanted lines). Two short sentences ending in '...' stand in for all of it, and I cannot find these sentences in the margins.
ocr_errors.problem: Nearly all of the printed marginal text is dropped, and what replaces it looks invented. This marginal commentary is part of the lithograph, not a later hand, though the OCR's warning calls it handwritten marginalia.

book_verdict: The leaf is right, but the OCR keeps only the first few rows of each column. It drops almost all of the extensive printed marginal text and fills the lower table with looping invented entries, and the translation turns all of that into fluent glossary English. The glosses are accurate; the transcription under them is not.
